preferred_option.text: Among the recorded alternatives (neutral labels; details are quoted data), which one is best supported by the recorded trade-offs? Choose NONE_CLEAR if the recorded material does not separate them.

criteria.NONE_CLEAR: the recorded material does not clearly favour one alternative

decision_supported.text: The recorded Decision is supported by the recorded comparison and rationale.
decision_supported.instructions: Read the recorded Decision together with the recorded comparison and rationale. Answer true only if the comparison and rationale recorded in the same record actually support the chosen alternative. A decision that rests on facts not in the record, or that contradicts the recorded trade-offs, is not supported.

true.what: Yes: the recorded comparison and rationale support the recorded Decision.
examples: Decision picks option B; the recorded comparison shows B has the lowest cost and the rationale cites that cost

false.what: No: the recorded Decision is not backed by the recorded comparison and rationale, or contradicts them.
examples: Decision picks option B, but the recorded comparison lists B's cost as the highest and gives no other reason

owner_calls_resolved.text: Every recorded Owner Call carries a human answer (status resolved), as opposed to an open question.
owner_calls_resolved.instructions: Check every recorded Owner Call. Answer true only if each one carries a human answer (status resolved). If any Owner Call is still an open question, or the answer was filled in by an agent rather than a human, answer false.

true.what: Yes: every recorded Owner Call has a human answer with status resolved.
examples: Two Owner Calls are listed and both show status resolved with the owner's answer text

false.what: No: at least one recorded Owner Call is still an open question, or its answer was not given by a human.
examples: One Owner Call shows status open with no answer

tradeoff_completeness.text: How complete is the recorded trade-off material for the chosen alternative?

criteria.label: partial
criteria.description: some pros/cons, no costs or no basis

criteria.label: mostly
criteria.description: pros/cons and costs, basis partially cited

criteria.label: complete
criteria.description: pros/cons, costs and cited basis for every alternative

failure_category.text: Classify the recorded failure into exactly one category.

criteria.SPEC: the specification or acceptance criteria are missing or contradictory
criteria.IMPL: implementation defect within the task's own code
criteria.UNKNOWN: the recorded material does not allow a classification

retry_same_tier_useful.text: A retry at the same model tier is likely to resolve the recorded failure.
retry_same_tier_useful.instructions: Read the recorded failure and decide whether running the same task again at the same model tier is likely to resolve it. Answer true for transient or sampling-dependent failures (a flaky run, a near miss). Answer false for failures that point to a missing spec, a broken environment or a defect a retry would repeat.

true.what: Yes: the failure looks transient or near-miss, so a retry at the same model tier is likely to resolve it.
examples: Test run failed once on a timeout and the same task passed on earlier attempts

false.what: No: the failure is systematic (missing spec, broken environment, repeated defect), so a retry at the same tier would fail the same way.
examples: The same assertion failed on every attempt because the spec contradicts itself
